title: Biopsychosocial and Cultural Determinants of Functioning and Healthcare Outcomes in Chronic Non-Cancer Pain: An Integrative Review
authors: Rocío Cáceres-Matos; Miguel Garrido-Bueno; Juan Manuel Fernández-Sarmiento; Ana María Porcel-Gálvez; Manuel Pabón-Carrasco; Daniele Giansanti
pain_condition_detail: chronic non-cancer pain (CNCP), including musculoskeletal pain, temporomandibular disorder, shoulder pain, lumbar pain
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses the BPS model as an organizing framework to structure its thematic synthesis into biological, psychological, social, and cultural themes. It describes interactions between domains (e.g., sleep disturbance with emotional health, social support with pain intensity) but does not specify mechanistic pathways. The model is invoked to justify multidimensional assessment and person-centered care.
integration_mechanism_summary: The paper asserts bidirectional interactions between biological and psychological domains (e.g., sleep disturbance with emotional health) and directional effects of social support on psychological distress. It describes a triadic mutual shaping but does not specify a mechanistic pathway linking all three domains. The fear-avoidance model is invoked as an explanatory mechanism for the bio-psych pathway.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper asserts a biopsychosocial model but organizes results into five parallel themes, with integration discussed only in a separate section
conceptual_tensions_2: Social determinants are acknowledged as important but the evidence reviewed is described as concentrating on biomedical and psychological dimensions
conceptual_tensions_3: The fear-avoidance model is invoked as a mechanism but only covers bio-psych pathways, not social factors
additional_observations_1: The paper uses nursing taxonomies (NANDA-I) to operationalize experiential domains, which is an unusual operationalization strategy
additional_observations_2: The review includes cultural factors as a separate dimension but does not elaborate them in the results, they are mentioned in the introduction and discussion
additional_observations_3: The paper explicitly excludes review articles to avoid duplication, which limits the depth of synthesis on mechanisms
synthesis_note: This integrative review uses the BPS model as an organizing framework to structure a thematic synthesis of 44 studies on CNCP. Psychological factors are elaborated (resilience, depression, catastrophizing, fear-avoidance), while biological and social factors are mentioned but not developed. Integration is asserted as reciprocal but remains at the level of directional claims without mechanistic pathways. The paper self-critiques the literature's imbalance toward biomedical and psychological dimensions.
coding_rationale: Typology 'multifactorial' because all three domains are present but treated in parallel themes; triadic integration 'partial' because bio-psych and psych-social links are directional but social-bio links are only descriptive. Psychological domain is elaborated; biological and social are mentioned. The BPS label is used as an organizing principle and explanatory framework.

title: Biopsychosocial and Cultural Determinants of Functioning and Healthcare Outcomes in Chronic Non-Cancer Pain: An Integrative Review
authors: Rocío Cáceres-Matos; Miguel Garrido-Bueno; Juan Manuel Fernández-Sarmiento; Ana María Porcel-Gálvez; Manuel Pabón-Carrasco; Daniele Giansanti
pain_condition_detail: Chronic non-cancer pain (CNCP), including musculoskeletal CNCP, shoulder pain, temporomandibular disorder (TMD), lumbar CNCP, osteoarthritis-related pain, and generalized CNCP.
context_note: European and Spanish prevalence estimates; high-income country predominance with implications for low- and middle-income settings; English/Spanish-only evidence.
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses BPS mainly as an organizing and explanatory frame for an integrative review: it extracts biological, psychological, social, and cultural attributes and synthesizes themes, then argues reciprocal interaction. It does not specify a formal BPS measurement model or causal SEM; social content is acknowledged as underexplored.
integration_mechanism_summary: Proposes reciprocal shaping of biological vulnerability, psychological regulation, functional capacity, and social context. Fear-avoidance pathway: pain-related fear -> activity avoidance -> deconditioning -> disability. Social support mitigates emotional distress and pain interference; relational strain/social isolation amplify burden. No formal mediator or quantitative causal model.
quality_assessment_tools_2: scottish intercollegiate guidelines network (sign) levels of evidence framework
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper argues reciprocal BPS interaction, but the evidence base is mostly cross-sectional or observational, limiting causal inference
conceptual_tensions_2: All three domains are integrated in synthesis, yet the authors report social determinants and healthcare quality as underexplored
conceptual_tensions_3: Chronic pain is framed as an ICD-11 diagnostic entity, but included studies vary in operational definitions of chronic pain
conceptual_tensions_4: Social determinants are central to the BPS account, but included evidence is predominately high-income, limiting transferability
conceptual_tensions_5: Clinical practice is described as fragmented and pharmacological despite evidence supporting integrated care
additional_observations_1: The review treats cultural aspects as socially shared meanings and norms, but does not operationalize spirituality or existential suffering
additional_observations_2: Search terms include nursing diagnostic labels such as impaired sleep pattern, impaired mood regulation, and hypervigilance to pain as sensitizing concepts
additional_observations_3: Grey literature search yielded no relevant results to be included in the review
additional_observations_4: The abstract repeats Background and Results paragraphs
additional_observations_5: SAGER guidelines are used for gender reporting, but no gender analysis tool is named
additional_observations_6: Quantitative findings are descriptively summarized and mapped to themes, qualitative data are interpretively synthesized
synthesis_note: The paper presents a genuinely integrative BPS account: it synthesizes biological, psychological, social, and cultural determinants and argues reciprocal interaction. However, its operationalization is thematic and narrative rather than measured or causal; social content is acknowledged as underexplored and much evidence is cross-sectional.
coding_rationale: All three domains are substantively present and linked reciprocally in the narrative, so typology is true_integrative. Integration is mechanistic for bio-psych and psych-social through fear-avoidance and support pathways; triadic integration is descriptive because no formal mediator is specified.

title: Biopsychosocial and Cultural Determinants of Functioning and Healthcare Outcomes in Chronic Non-Cancer Pain: An Integrative Review
authors: Rocío Cáceres-Matos; Miguel Garrido-Bueno; Juan Manuel Fernández-Sarmiento; Ana María Porcel-Gálvez; Manuel Pabón-Carrasco; Daniele Giansanti
pain_condition_detail: Chronic non-cancer pain (CNCP) in adults, including musculoskeletal, widespread, and other persistent pain conditions.
context_note: Studies published in English and Spanish, with some focus on rural populations and gender differences.
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; explanatory framework; organizing principle
bps_operationalization_summary: Organizes findings into five thematic domains (biological, functioning/QoL, psychological, social support, social/gender determinants) and argues for their interaction within a BPS framework, though integration is described rather than mechanistically specified.
integration_mechanism_summary: The paper proposes a descriptive triadic integration where biological vulnerability, psychological regulation, functional capacity, and social context continuously shape one another reciprocally. Directional relationships are specified between domains, but no mechanistic pathways are detailed.
conceptual_tensions_1: Tension between academic recognition of BPS multidimensional nature and clinical practice's continued biomedical focus
conceptual_tensions_2: Tension between descriptive triadic integration and lack of mechanistic pathways explaining domain interactions
conceptual_tensions_3: Tension between evidence on social determinants and their underrepresentation in existing literature
conceptual_tensions_4: Tension between cross-sectional study designs limiting causal inference and the need for longitudinal understanding of BPS interactions
additional_observations_1: The review uses integrative methodology to synthesize both quantitative and qualitative evidence through convergent thematic synthesis
additional_observations_2: Gender is treated as a cross-cutting determinant with specific mention of gender-based discrimination and women's experience of pain as 'bodily protest'
additional_observations_3: Rural residence is identified as a specific contextual factor associated with higher CNCP prevalence
additional_observations_4: The review explicitly excludes cancer-related pain and cognitive impairment populations, focusing specifically on CNCP in adults
additional_observations_5: Cultural aspects are interpreted as 'socially shared meanings and norms through which chronic pain is understood and experienced'
synthesis_note: This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of CNCP evidence using an integrative approach, explicitly framing the condition through a biopsychosocial lens. It elaborates all three core domains with substantial constructs and identifies directional relationships between them, though integration remains descriptive rather than mechanistic. The review identifies key conceptual problems including underrepresentation of social determinants and healthcare quality, and a gap between academic recognition and clinical implementation of BPS principles. The evidence base is strengthened by systematic appraisal using SIGN and JBI tools, though limitations include cross-sectional designs and high-income country
coding_rationale: Scored as 'elaborated' for all three core domains based on multiple named constructs and sustained discussion. Triadic integration rated 'descriptive' because domains are related reciprocally but no specific mechanistic pathways are detailed. BPS typology 'multifactorial' because all domains are substantively present but treated as interacting rather than fully integrated mechanisms.

bps_usage_instances_01_usage_verbatim: The integrative synthesis of the evidence included in this review consolidates chronic non-cancer pain (CNCP) as a dynamic, multidimensional, and socially embedded condition that is most appropriately understood through the biopsychosocial model.
bps_usage_instances_01_note: Positions BPS as the appropriate framework for understanding CNCP.
bps_usage_instances_02_usage_verbatim: Rather than resulting from isolated biological dysfunction, CNCP emerges from the continuous and reciprocal interaction among biological vulnerability, psychological regulation, functional capacity, and social context.
bps_usage_instances_02_note: Describes the interaction mechanism of BPS domains.
bps_usage_instances_03_usage_verbatim: This integrative review synthesized and analyzed existing evidence on the biological, psychological, social, and cultural dimensions characterizing individuals with CNCP, and their impact on functionality, quality of life, and healthcare.
bps_usage_instances_03_note: Frames the study objective using BPS language.
bps_usage_instances_04_usage_verbatim: Within this framework, the fear-avoidance model provides a robust explanatory lens, suggesting that pain-related fear leads to activity avoidance, progressive deconditioning, and disability, thereby sustaining the chronic pain cycle.
bps_usage_instances_04_note: Uses BPS to contextualize fear-avoidance model application.
bps_usage_instances_05_usage_verbatim: Such an approach is consistent with contemporary interdisciplinary and person-centered models of chronic pain care.
theoretical_frameworks_01_framework_verb: This integrative review synthesized and analyzed existing evidence on the biological, psychological, social, and cultural dimensions characterizing individuals with CNCP, and their impact on functionality, quality of life, and healthcare. In particular, the review focuses on identifying key biopsychosocial determinants and consequences associated with CNCP and how these influence functional outcomes and care experiences.
theoretical_frameworks_02_framework_verb: Within this framework, the fear-avoidance model provides a robust explanatory lens, suggesting that pain-related fear leads to activity avoidance, progressive deconditioning, and disability, thereby sustaining the chronic pain cycle.
theoretical_frameworks_03_framework_verb: The framework proposed by Whittemore and Knafl was therefore adopted to support a comprehensive and structured synthesis of heterogeneous evidence.
theoretical_frameworks_04_framework_verb: The research question was structured using the Person, Exposure, Outcome (PEO) framework, a widely recognized variant of the PICO model, which facilitated the identification of defining attributes.
theoretical_frameworks_05_framework_verb: The review adhered to the recommendations of the Sex and Gender Equity in Research (SAGER) guidelines to ensure the appropriate consideration of gender aspects in the reporting process.
theoretical_frameworks_06_framework_verb: Moreover, social determinants, including socioeconomic status, social support, and working conditions, play a decisive role in pain experience and access to care, consistent with emerging multilevel and life-course perspectives on pain inequities.
theoretical_frameworks_08_framework_verb: Person-centered nursing frameworks, such as the Self-Care and Adaptation models, provide conceptual tools for integrating emotional, behavioral, and environmental dimensions into pain management.
instruments_01_construct_measured_as_sta: methodological rigor and strength of evidence of the included studies
instruments_01_instrument_verbatim: The methodological rigor and strength of evidence of the included studies were assessed using the Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN) levels of evidence framework.
instruments_02_construct_measured_as_sta: quality or risk-of-bias assessment of the evidence
instruments_02_instrument_verbatim: Studies were screened using predefined eligibility criteria and appraised with Joanna Briggs Institute tools.
conceptual_problems_01_problem_verbatim: Evidence largely concentrates on biomedical, functional, and psychological dimensions, whereas social determinants and healthcare quality remain comparatively underexplored.
conceptual_problems_01_note: Authors identify underrepresentation of social determinants and healthcare quality in existing evidence.
conceptual_problems_02_problem_verbatim: Biological mechanisms alone are insufficient to explain its chronification or the degree of disability it produces.
conceptual_problems_02_note: Authors note lack of mechanistic explanation for biological-psychological integration.
conceptual_problems_03_problem_verbatim: Although academic discourse increasingly recognizes the multidimensional nature of CNCP, clinical practice remains largely biomedical and fragmented, emphasizing pharmacological management with limited interdisciplinary coordination.
conceptual_problems_03_note: Clinical practice reduces BPS to biomedical focus despite academic recognition.
conceptual_problems_04_problem_verbatim: The limited inclusion of qualitative studies may have reduced the interpretative depth regarding the subjective experience of pain and its sociocultural dimensions.
conceptual_problems_04_note: Measurement approach may not capture subjective social and psychological experience.
conceptual_problems_05_affected_labels: rural populations | low- and middle-income settings
conceptual_problems_05_problem_verbatim: Another relevant limitation is the predominance of studies conducted in high-income countries, which may restrict the transferability of findings to different sociocultural contexts.
conceptual_problems_05_note: Limited generalizability to different socioeconomic contexts.
key_quotes_01_claim_verbatim: Rather than resulting from isolated biological dysfunction, CNCP emerges from the continuous and reciprocal interaction among biological vulnerability, psychological regulation, functional capacity, and social context.
key_quotes_01_why_it_matters: Positions CNCP as an integrated biopsychosocial phenomenon rather than isolated dysfunction.
key_quotes_02_claim_verbatim: Evidence largely concentrates on biomedical, functional, and psychological dimensions, whereas social determinants and healthcare quality remain comparatively underexplored.
key_quotes_02_why_it_matters: Identifies gap in social determinants coverage in existing literature.
key_quotes_03_claim_verbatim: Within this framework, the fear-avoidance model provides a robust explanatory lens, suggesting that pain-related fear leads to activity avoidance, progressive deconditioning, and disability, thereby sustaining the chronic pain cycle.
key_quotes_03_why_it_matters: Applies fear-avoidance model within BPS framework to explain disability cycle.
key_quotes_04_claim_verbatim: Biological mechanisms contribute to pain persistence, and psychological distress, coping patterns, and social conditions appear to play a central role in shaping functional outcomes.
key_quotes_04_why_it_matters: Establishes relative importance of psychological and social factors for outcomes.
key_quotes_05_claim_verbatim: Socioeconomic disadvantages and environmental constraints were linked to higher pain burden, whereas resilience and social support emerged as protective factors mitigating functional and psychosocial impact.
key_quotes_05_why_it_matters: Demonstrates protective role of social factors against pain burden.
key_quotes_06_claim_verbatim: Although academic discourse increasingly recognizes the multidimensional nature of CNCP, clinical practice remains largely biomedical and fragmented, emphasizing pharmacological management with limited interdisciplinary coordination.
key_quotes_06_why_it_matters: Highlights gap between academic recognition and clinical implementation of BPS.
